ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory positive-match screening against the United Nations Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury (Sanctions) List, and any applicable New Zealand sanctions measures under the Sanctions Act 2020. All directors, UBOs, authorized signatories, and counterparties engaged in corporate Scope 1–3 carbon auditing and offset brokerage must be screened prior to incorporation and on a continuous risk-based basis. PEPs, close associates, and family members are subject to enhanced due diligence (EDD) and approval by a senior compliance officer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office (Na t he Companies Office), part of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), accessible via https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in English using Latin script characters, including Māori words and macrons (e.g., ā, ē, ī, ō, ū). Non-Latin script is not accepted for statutory registration; transliteration into Latin script is required. Names must not be identical or almost identical to an existing or reserved name, and must end with the word 'Limited' (or its approved abbreviation 'Ltd') for ordinary limited liability companies.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 working days of a rejection notice issued by the Companies Office, the applicant may file a written Request for Reconsideration via the Companies Office portal, quoting the reference number and addressing the stated grounds of refusal. If the reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may file a formal administrative appeal to the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), and thereafter may initiate judicial review proceedings in the High Court of New Zealand under the Companies Act 1993 and the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016. A new reservation application may also be submitted with revised terms; priority over a conflicting name will only be granted through a validly reserved name number.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are accepted for the statutory registered office address only where the provider maintains a physical street address in New Zealand and personnel are available to receive service of process during ordinary business hours. A mere postal box or shell address is not permissible. A virtual office is commonly used for ESG carbon accounting and advisory firms where no physical occupancy is required, provided the company can demonstrate a verifiable physical presence and access to corporate records at the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate for the first year of operation; approximate 15% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the AML/CFT reporting entity supervisor (e.g., the Financial Markets Authority or Department of Internal Affairs) or the Companies Registry for standard-risk carbon consultancy and brokerage activities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), ss 10-14 (incorporation and registration), s 15 (company name), s 16 (registered office), ss 26-27 (constitution contract), ss 91 and 103 (written resolutions), ss 151-152 (directors and residency), s 189 (accounting records), and Schedule 2 (constitution default rules); New Zealand Business Number Act 2016, s 7 (NZBN allocation); Financial Reporting Act 2013 (reporting and assurance framework); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (banking counterparty due diligence)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Te Ahua o te Kamupene), a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the Companies Register and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) registry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Application for Incorporation of a Company, filed electronically through the Companies Register portal (business.govt.nz / companiesoffice.govt.nz), resulting in a Certificate of Incorporation issued under s 13 of the Companies Act 1993
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies in New Zealand; a company may be incorporated with one or more shares issued for cash, partly paid, or non-cash consideration without escrow or capital deposit accounts. For this entity, one ordinary share of NZD 1.00 is subscribed and paid at allotment to establish membership and solvency, with further shares issuable by board resolution under s 99 of the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: MINUTES OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME LIMITED] held on [Date] at [Time] at [Registered Office Address], New Zealand. Present: [Director 1], Chair; [Director 2], Director; [Company Secretary], Secretary. 1. INCORPORATION: The Board ratified the incorporation of the Company under the Companies Act 1993, the filing of Form 1, the issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, and the allocation of the New Zealand Business Number. 2. SHARE CAPITAL: The Board approved the issue and allotment of 1 ordinary share of NZD 1.00 to [Founding Shareholder] at par, fully paid, and directed entry of the allotment in the Share Register and issuance of a share certificate. 3. CONSTITUTION: The Board adopted the Company's Constitution (or, in its absence, the default rules in Schedule 2 of the Companies Act 1993), and resolved that the Constitution shall bind the Company, each shareholder, each director, and the Company Secretary as a statutory contract under ss 26-27. 4. REGISTERED OFFICE AND ADDRESS FOR SERVICE: The registered office and address for service are fixed at [Street Address, City, New Zealand], which is open to the public on business days, and the Board directed lodgment of the notice of registered office under s 16. 5. DIRECTOR RESIDENCY AND OFFICERS: The Board confirmed that at least one director resident in New Zealand is maintained pursuant to s 152, appointed [Director 1] as Chief Executive Officer, [Director 2] as Chief Financial Officer, and resolved that the Company Secretary, if any, need not be an officer under the Act. 6. BANK MANDATE: The Board authorised the opening of corporate operating and SWIFT wire-capable foreign currency accounts with a registered New Zealand bank, approved the authorised signatories, and ratified the account mandate for Swift_Wire and wire transfer rails. 7. TAX AND ACCOUNTING: Management was directed to apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number, GST registration if annual turnover is expected to exceed NZD 60,000, and to maintain proper accounting records under s 189 consistent with NZ IFRS and the GHG Protocol for the Company's own Scope 1-3 emissions. 8. LICENSING AND ENVIRONMENTAL: The Board authorised the application for a holding account on the New Zealand Emissions Trading Register through the Environmental Protection Authority, registration with voluntary carbon standards, and implementation of the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 plan and building warrant of fitness compliance. RESOLVED: That all actions, appointments, and authorisations in these minutes are confirmed and ratified, and any director or officer is authorised to execute agreements and file statutory forms to give full effect to these resolutions. All resolutions passed unanimously. Signed: [Chair]. Minutes recorded: [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Search, Reservation, and Director Consent Collection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Register online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search through the Companies Register to ensure the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing New Zealand or overseas registered name under ss 15-18 of the Companies Act 1993. Reserve the chosen name, if required, and collect executed Consent to Act as Director forms from each proposed director, together with certified identity documents. Confirm at least one director is resident in New Zealand, or qualifies as an Australian resident director of an Australian company under the s 152 exemption.
required_dossiers: Signed Consent to Act as Director forms
Certified passport or national identity card of each director and shareholder
Director residential address and service address details
Name reservation confirmation (if obtained)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected under s 16 or 18 on the grounds of being offensive or confusingly similar, file a fresh application using an alternative relatively distinctive name or submit written submissions to the Registrar for reconsideration. A decision may also be challenged by judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016 within 30 days if procedural unfairness is established.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Constitution and Preparation of the Incorporation Application Pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and circulate the Company Constitution (voluntary) or elect to rely on the Schedule 2 default constitution rules. Draft Form 1 Application for Incorporation containing the company name, business purpose (Corporate Scope 1-3 Carbon Footprint Auditing and Offset Brokerage - ISIC 7020 / NAICS 541620), share structure and classes, registered office, address for service, director particulars, and shareholder details. No notarisation is generally required for domestic incorporation; however, foreign-incorporated shareholders must provide certified English translations and apostilled copies of identity documents.
required_dossiers: Draft Form 1 - Application for Incorporation
Company Constitution (adopted as a separate instrument or incorporated by reference)
Subscriber declaration and share allotment plan
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or owner's consent letter)
Consent to Act as Director forms for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Registrar requests further information under s 10(2) of the Companies Act 1993, the applicant must respond within 14 days with clarifications or amendments. Errors in the draft Form 1 can be cured by resubmission of a corrected application before the payment stage; if already filed, an 'amend application' can be lodged online without incurring a new fee except where the company name is changed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission, Payment of Incorporation Fee, and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies / New Zealand Companies Office; New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the completed Form 1 and supporting dossiers on the Companies Register electronic portal and pay the prescribed registration fee of approximately NZD 105 (USD 65) via credit card or online account debit. Upon successful registration, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, a unique New Zealand company number, and a 13-digit New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) under the New Zealand Business Number Act 2016. The registered agent will immediately download the digital certificate and archive it in the company's statutory records folder.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Form 1 (electronic)
Payment confirmation reference (NZD 105 fee)
Constitution and consent forms (uploaded as attachments, if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the electronic filing is flagged with a 'Requires Attention' notice, correct the indicated data fields via the Companies Office portal within 10 working days. Rejected payments are retried automatically on the platform; in the case of an erroneous rejection, contact the Companies Office contact centre to obtain a manual BPAY reference, and if formal refusal occurs after filing, the applicant may apply under s 361 for administrative correction or seek judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with Inland Revenue: IRD Number, GST, PAYE and NRWT
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake), New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, register the company with Inland Revenue using the business gateway (ird.govt.nz) and the NZBN. Apply for a New Zealand IRD number, GST registration if the projected 12-month turnover equals or exceeds NZD 60,000, PAYE/ESCT if employees are engaged, and NRWT if foreign shareholders will receive dividends. Provide the registered office, bank account details, industry classification of ESG advisory and carbon accounting, and details of any foreign tax residence status. Maintain the IRD records to support the 'Tax_Exempt_Zone' classification and cross-border wire activity.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Company bank account confirmation
Certified passports of directors and beneficial owners
Projected turnover and business plan
IRD forms IR881 or IR742 for overseas tax residence status
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: IRD registration is typically completed instantly online, but if verification delays occur, call the IRD business helpline (0800 377 774) or file paper form IR596 with certified identity documents. Incorrect industrial classification or GST election can be amended through the 'Amend my registration' function, with effective date corrections backdated to the original registration date where a written objection is lodged within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convening of First Board Meeting, Share Certificate Issuance, and Establishment of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company; records maintained at the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting (or execute a written resolution under s 103 of the Companies Act 1993) and adopt the pro forma first board resolution. Approve the allotment of shares, issue and sign the share certificates, appoint the CEO, CFO, and if required the Company Secretary, and confirm the bank mandate. Open the statutory registers, including the Share Register, Director Register, Director Interests Register, and shareholder communications register, and maintain the minute book at the registered office. The share register must contain the name, address, number of shares, class, amount paid and transfer history of each shareholder.
required_dossiers: Signed board resolution minutes (or written resolution)
Share certificate for 1 ordinary share issued
Statutory register index (share, director and interests registers)
Notice of registered office and address for service
Annually updated Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defects in the minutes or share certificates are cured by a correcting resolution at the next board meeting or by a written resolution executed by all directors. Lost or destroyed statutory registers may be reconstructed by application to the Registrar under s 217 of the Companies Act 1993; late annual returns are remedied by filing online with the late-filing penalty of NZD 10 per month or part month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Bank Facilities, AML/KYC Onboarding, and Environmental/Emissions Registry Access
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered New Zealand banks under the AML/CFT Act 2009 and the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for bank supervision; Environmental Protection Authority (Te Mana Rauhī Taiao) for the New Zealand Emissions Trading Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a comprehensive corporate KYC pack to a registered New Zealand bank (e.g., ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Westpac) to open the operating account and a SWIFT wire-capable foreign currency account. Provide the bank with the certificate of incorporation, board resolution, director/shareholder passports, source of funds statements, and FATCA/CRS residence declarations. Simultaneously, apply to the Environmental Protection Authority for a holding account on the New Zealand Emissions Trading Register using the entity's NZBN; that account will permit client offset activity, unit transfers and brokerage settlement of NZUs and voluntary carbon credits. Maintain the AML/CFT risk rating as 'Low_Risk_Standard' and adopt a risk-based compliance programme.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN confirmation
Extract of board resolution approving bank signatories
Passports, proof of address, and source of wealth statements for all directors and beneficial owners
AML/CFT customer due diligence questionnaire
EPA New Zealand Emissions Trading Register holding account application (EPA-A1) and registration certificate
Business plan detailing carbon footprint audit and offset brokerage services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a 'non-client' notice under AML/CFT procedures, remediate by providing a solicitor referral letter, six-month source-of-funds statements, and an updated compliance policy; alternatively, apply to a second-tier registered bank (e.g., Heartland Bank or Rabobank) or a licensed non-bank deposit taker. For the EPA holding account, respond to the EPA's information query within 20 working days; full refusal may be appealed to the District Court under s 30ZG of the Climate Change Response Act 2002.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Environmental Protection Authority (Te Mana Rauhī Taiao), New Zealand, in coordination with the Ministry for the Environment (MfE) for climate reporting standards
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Non-licensed professional services status - no statutory operating permit required for corporate carbon footprint auditing and offset brokerage; recommended registrations include the EPA New Zealand Emissions Trading Register holding account and voluntary carbon standard programme membership (e.g., Verra VCS, Puro.earth)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (Te Mana Rauhī Taiao), New Zealand
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based administrative services under the Resource Management Act 1991 (Schedule 4 Part 2 categories); no industrial process, no contaminant discharge, and no significant environmental footprint; no project-level EIA required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality 2004 for any VOC-emitting office equipment (none in standard operations); office waste handled under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and local council waste by-laws; no wastewater discharge requiring a discharge consent; the firm's own operations must conform to ISO 14064-1 and the GHG Protocol Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard for Scope 1-3 calculation, and client deliverables must meet the ISO 14064-3 verification framework.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupational health and safety clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 (HSWA), including a written HSWA policy, hazard register, emergency evacuation plan, first aid provisions, and appointment of a health and safety officer; building warrant of fitness (BWOF) per the Building Act 2004 and Building (Earthquake-prone Buildings) Amendment Act 2016 for the leased premises, including fire alarm and automatic sprinkler system verification; Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) fire evacuation scheme approval for premises holding more than 100 persons under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017; civil defence emergency preparedness plan aligned with the National Civil Defence Emergency Management Plan 2015; and mandatory ACC (Accident Compensation Corporation) employer registration for worker injury cover.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand; statutory self-service portal is myIR operated at https://www.ird.govt.nz (including myIR secure online services for corporate taxpayers and agents).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign entity such as an International Company (IC) without a New Zealand permanent establishment: (1) apply for an IRD number using Form IR596 (Application by a company for an IRD number) or via myIR after creating a non-resident company profile; attach certified certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, registered office address, and beneficial ownership declaration; (2) appoint a New Zealand agent for service of process where no physical place of business exists; (3) register for GST using Form GST1 or myIR GST application only when a taxable activity in New Zealand is carried on and annual turnover exceeds NZD 60,000, or on a voluntary basis for business-to-business supplies and cross-border remote services; (4) rely on the New Zealand tax-exempt zone classification for offshore-source income, maintaining a zero income tax filing obligation while retaining any necessary GST registration solely for New Zealand-source supplies of goods and services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not recognise the United States-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections relevant to an International Company include: (a) Look-Through Company (LTC) election under section HB 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007, rendering an eligible New Zealand-resident company fiscally transparent for income tax purposes; (b) Qualifying Company election under the Companies Act 1993 transitional rules (closed to new elections since 1 April 2010); (c) consolidated group election under sections HB 1-HB 4 of the Income Tax Act 2007, permitting group aggregation for tax purposes; (d) GST group registration election under section 55 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; and (e) hybrid mismatch and branch mismatch elections under the hybrid rules in Part 4B of the Income Tax Act 2007 for structured cross-border arrangements, where a foreign entity tax classification may be disregarded or re-characterised in accordance with the OECD BEPS hybrid framework.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 annual taxable turnover (12-month rolling basis); the same threshold applies to non-resident suppliers of remote services and low-value imported goods supplied to New Zealand consumers, where registration is compulsory if total cross-border supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance regime, no tax-authority API pre-clearance, and no digital stamping obligation. New Zealand operates a voluntary Peppol-compliant e-invoicing network administered through the E-Invoicing NZ framework; e-invoices must be issued and retained in a format accessible to IRD on request, but there is no continuous transaction control or pre-approval by the Inland Revenue Department.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for New Zealand GST applies to: (a) goods exported by the supplier within 28 days of supply, provided the goods do not subsequently return to New Zealand or are not subjected to a taxable supply in New Zealand; (b) services supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time services are performed, where the recipient acquires the services for the purposes of a business carried on outside New Zealand; and (c) offshore services performed outside New Zealand. For an ESG carbon accounting and offset brokerage company selling audit advisory services to non-resident clients, zero-rating requires clear documentary evidence that the recipient is non-resident, the supply is consumed outside New Zealand, and no New Zealand land or goods remain within New Zealand. Carbon offset brokerage services may be zero-rated only if the underlying offset units are recognised as exported intangible services; IRD may recharacterise brokerage fees as New Zealand-sourced if the contract negotiations, risk management, or legal performance occur in New Zealand.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: NZCS Customs Export Declaration (Electronic Declaration / TPP exit declaration)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank SWIFT confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the non-resident customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Inland Revenue Department and New Zealand Customs Service jointly audit zero-rating claims. Exporters are liable to repay any GST input tax credits recovered on goods or services that are not exported within the statutory timeframe or that are subsequently reimported or diverted to a taxable use in New Zealand; use-of-money interest applies on all clawed-back amounts. Civil shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply up to 150% of the resulting tax shortfall in cases of abusive tax positions or evasion, and an additional 100% penalty may be imposed for fraudulent or wilful acts under section 141E of the Tax Administration Act 1994. Criminal prosecution under section 144A of the Tax Administration Act 1994 and section 253 of the Crimes Act 1961 can lead to imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines of up to NZD 50,000 for an individual or NZD 250,000 for a company. In practice, IRD applies retrospective reassessment for up to four years, extended to ten years in cases of evasion or fraudulent activity involving export zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua), operating under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021; the Monetary Policy Committee sets monetary policy, while the Reserve Bank jointly supervises banks with the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) compliance. No separate Foreign Exchange Administration exists because New Zealand has no exchange-control statute.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and free convertibility on both current and capital account under the freely floating New Zealand dollar (NZD). There are no exchange-control approvals, no capital-account licensing, and no restrictions on profit or dividend repatriation, loan repayment, or liquidation remittances to non-resident shareholders. The only regulatory gates are the Overseas Investment Act 2018 for acquisitions of sensitive land or significant business assets (not engaged by an ISIC 7020 ESG carbon audit and offset brokerage company), the Companies Act 1993 overseas-company registration requirement if the entity carries on business in New Zealand, and bank-level AML/CFT and sanctions screening. Profit remittance from New Zealand is subject to non-resident dividend or interest withholding tax under the Income Tax Act 2007, reduced only where an applicable double tax agreement provides relief; the Cook Islands International Company's exempt-zone tax classification does not automatically eliminate New Zealand-source withholding.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. New Zealand does not impose any statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts or service fee income; foreign currency export proceeds and professional fee receivables may be retained offshore or onshore in any currency without surrender. The only ongoing obligations are accurate reporting to the Reserve Bank for Balance of Payments statistics and compliance with the AML/CFT Act 2009 record-retention rules. The corporate Scope 1-3 carbon auditing and offset brokerage service revenue is treated as service export income, fully fungible and freely usable for treasury purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Multi-Currency Account (NZD, USD, EUR, GBP, AUD, CNH)
Operational Account with foreign-currency holding and FX-forward access
Operational Account with cash-pooling, escrow services, and treasury dealing line
Operational Account with daily dealing and cross-currency account
Global Multi-Currency Operating Account with notional cash pooling

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Conditional Medium-High. New Zealand does not maintain a standalone e-money institution (EMI) licensing category; non-bank payment providers must operate through a registered bank partner for settlement and are supervised for AML/CFT purposes by the Financial Markets Authority or the Reserve Bank. Offshore digital EMIs (UK FCA-authorised, Australian AFSL/ACL holders, or Singapore MPI holders) cannot hold on-balance-sheet NZD deposits or issue NZD e-money in New Zealand without a local banking/AML/CFT registration; they may, however, be used as a supplementary disbursement rail for small retail carbon offset micro-purchases through master-account arrangements. The CK_IC should maintain its primary treasury and clearing relationship with an NZ tier-1 bank and use an offshore EMI only as a secondary, non-critical channel subject to a group treasury policy cap.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory face-to-face KYC interview. New Zealand tier-1 banks will not open an account for a Cook Islands International Company by fully remote means; at least one director (or a licensed New Zealand corporate director) must attend an in-person interview at a New Zealand branch, or exceptionally at an Australasian designated branch, with the remaining directors verified by live video call and notarised passport copies. Non-face-to-face onboarding is not practically available where the beneficial-owner chain contains tax-exempt-zone elements; the bank will additionally require a statement from a New Zealand-qualified lawyer confirming the director personal meetings, the substance of the Cook Islands IC, and the absence of nominee opacity. All customer due diligence must meet the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and the AML/CFT Regulations 2011 verification standards.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore shell-company pattern: a Cook Islands International Company with Tax-Exempt-zone classification, non-resident ownership, and possible nominee shareholding triggers enhanced due diligence and potential rejection at bank compliance review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing issued by the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission within 30 days; (2) current Statement of Directors, Statement of Members, and registered-address certificates from the licensed Cook Islands registered agent; (3) a statutory declaration that no bearer shares are outstanding and no bearer-share warrants exist; (4) a New Zealand tax opinion confirming non-resident status and the tax-exempt reasoning under section YD 2 of the Income Tax Act 2007 and any applicable double tax agreement between New Zealand and the Cook Islands; (5) a full group-structure chart with each natural-person UBO's passport copy and proof of address; (6) CRS/FATCA self-certifications and a signed AML/CFT beneficial-ownership questionnaire in the bank's prescribed form.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the initial treasury injection and shareholder loan funding, creating a potential suspicious transaction report under the AML/CFT Act 2009.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (1) a board resolution authorising the capital injection or loan and specifying the exact amount, currency, remitter, and purpose; (2) a notarised source-of-wealth report per contributing UBO with six months of bank statements, asset-sale contracts, or inheritance and probate documents; (3) a flows-matching schedule tying each inbound MT103 to its underlying commercial event; (4) a letter from a licensed New Zealand chartered accountant confirming the working-capital requirement for the ISIC 7020 carbon audit practice; (5) a signed declaration of source of funds consistent with the entity's stated ESG service operating budget.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Annual Return (AR) including confirmation of members, directors, shareholdings, and beneficial ownership particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 15 working days after the company's annual return date (the anniversary of incorporation or the date fixed by the Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: NZD 50 late filing penalty imposed on default; failure to file for two consecutive annual return periods exposes the company to administrative strike-off by the Registrar after formal notice; reinstatement is subject to court or Registrar approval and additional fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Statutory Audit Report (required where the entity qualifies as large or is a reporting entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, with copies tabled before shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Large reporting entities: file audited financial statements within 20 working days after the annual return date; non-reporting entities: prepare financial statements and supporting accounting records within 5 months after balance date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors commit an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 for non-preparation or non-filing, with fines and continuing daily penalties; persistent non-compliance supports Registrar strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual IRD Income Tax Return (including nil return or tax-exempt activity declaration where the International Company derives no assessable New Zealand-source income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Government of New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Standard 31 March balance date: return due by 7 July following the end of the income year; non-standard balance date: return due by the 7th day of the 7th month following balance date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Initial late filing penalty of NZD 250 plus monthly NZD 50 late filing penalties until filed, subject to statutory maximum; late payment interest and late payment penalties accrue at IRD rates; continued default may result in Commissioner-based assessment and enforcement action.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is mandatory where the company is 'large' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, i.e., it satisfies at least two of the following in each of the two preceding accounting periods: total assets exceeding NZD 10,000,000; total revenue exceeding NZD 20,000,000; or 50 or more full-time equivalent employees. Audit may also be required where shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares resolve to require it for a financial year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For-profit entities must prepare financial statements under New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP): Tier 1 full NZ IFRS; Tier 2 NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR); Tier 3 XRB A1 For-profit Simple Format Reporting; Tier 4 XRB A1 cash-basis standards, as applicable by size and public accountability.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual return date the company must verify and confirm the accuracy of the Register of Members and record any shareholding transfers. Under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) Amendment Act 2023, the company must take reasonable steps to identify every ultimate beneficial owner exercising 25% or more ownership or control, notify the Registrar of any change within 15 working days of becoming aware of the change, and reconfirm the UBO particulars annually with the return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Senior Managers
Register of Beneficial Ownership (25% or more UBO information)
Register of Share Transfers and Shareholdings
Minute Book (shareholders' and directors' meetings and resolutions)
